The work is evaluated against other resampling/synthetic data generation techniques on small tabular datasets. CTGAN is cited, likely as a comparison method, but the evidence does not confirm it was actually run.

It is a broad academic survey rather than an applied or software paper, citing over a hundred works across the vine copula literature. paper-privacy-preserving-network-securit.summary: This paper proposes system architectures and a design for privacy-preserving publication of network security log data, arguing that such logs carry sensor-data-level identifiability risks and proposing a risk-based approach to sanitized data publication for security analytics research. In its related work section it discusses the Synthetic Data Vault as an example of a system-oriented privacy preservation approach that generates synthetic relational data from models learned on public datasets. SDV is only described and cited as prior related work, not run or extended in this paper's own architecture.

paper-wind-copula-2015.summary: Pre-SDV copula work: estimates wind speed at candidate turbine sites from correlated reference sites using copula graphical models. The copula machinery here is the ancestor of the Copulas library and GaussianCopulaSynthesizer.

preprint-batterypass-12k-first-dataset-2.summary: This paper introduces BatteryPass-12K, the first public benchmark dataset for classifying digital battery passport (DBP) conformance to EU battery regulation, created synthetically from real pilot samples, and evaluates 22 language models on the task in zero-shot and few-shot settings. The SDV paper is listed among a string of general citations on synthetic data generation in machine learning and is not engaged with further; SDV's synthetic data vault concept is only cited, not used to produce the dataset.

preprint-causal-parametric-drift-simulat.summary: This paper proposes a Digital Twin framework using Structural Causal Models to simulate causal parametric drift for stress-testing classifier robustness, applied to the OSMI mental-health dataset and evaluated against statistical drift monitors and SHAP-based explanations. CTGAN is cited only briefly in the related-work discussion of deep generative models that achieve high-fidelity sampling of P(X,Y) but lack controlled causal interventions, contrasting with the authors' causal SCM approach. CTGAN is mentioned as a black-box generative baseline paradigm the paper positions itself against, but it is neither run nor benchmarked.

preprint-llm-discriminator-when-syntheti.summary: This paper proposes an LLM-based privacy audit method for tabular synthetic data, prompting LLaMA and Gemini to classify table samples as REAL or SYNTHETIC under two disclosure conditions and comparing the resulting Disclosure Risk Score against classifier two-sample tests, record linkage, and a human annotator pilot. The synthetic tables audited across UCI Adult and ACS Census are generated by CTGAN, TVAE, and Gaussian Copula run 'via the SDV framework with default hyperparameters,' making SDV's synthesizers the very objects the whole LLM-discrimination evaluation is built around.

paper-ctdgan-latent-subspaces-2025.summary: Proposes ctdGAN, a conditional tabular GAN that first clusters the training rows, then samples the latent space in proportion to cluster and class probabilities, conditioning the generator on both the class label and the cluster so that minority regions are reached without a separate oversampling step. It builds on CTGAN in two places, taking its dual generator output of a hyperbolic tangent for continuous values and a Gumbel softmax for discrete ones and the first two terms of its generator loss, while replacing CTGAN's variational Gaussian mixture normalization with a cluster-based scheme on the grounds that the mixture inflates dimensionality; CTGAN and TVAE are also among the compared generators.

paper-causal-hybrid-llm-synthetic-2025.summary: Shows that synthetic tabular data can score well on train-on-synthetic-test-on-real prediction while badly misestimating the average treatment effect, and proposes a hybrid generator that synthesises covariates with a generative model but fits propensity and outcome models separately, so the treatment and outcome structure is preserved; it adds a pairing strategy for positivity violations and uses the unlimited synthetic sample to benchmark IPTW, AIPW and substitution estimators. A GAN-based generator supplies half the results and CTGAN is the only tabular GAN the paper cites or describes, credited with mode-specific normalisation and training-by-sampling, but the GAN rows are never tied to a named implementation.

preprint-advancing-cardiovascular-diseas.summary: This preprint develops a machine learning ecosystem for cardiovascular disease diagnosis, combining tabular neural networks (TabNet, TabPFN, FT-Transformer) and ensemble models with interpretability (SHAP, counterfactuals), fairness auditing, uncertainty quantification, and causal inference to build a responsible AI framework validated on multi-regional heart disease datasets. The authors use CTGAN to generate synthetic instances that equalize disease frequency across sex subgroups for bias mitigation, and separately use the Gaussian Copula method to simulate a high-data augmentation scenario, ultimately finding both synthetic augmentation approaches degrade discriminative performance relative to real data. CTGAN's conditional generator and mode-specific normalization, and SDV's Gaussian Copula synthesizer, are both run as data augmentation methods within the empirical pipeline, evaluated as one of several techniques and found to have limitations.

preprint-boosting-predictive-performance.summary: The paper proposes a family of latent-space, tree-driven diffusion methods (PCAForest, EmbedForest, AttentionForest) that couple conditional flow matching with gradient-boosted trees for minority-class oversampling on tabular data, evaluated across 11 healthcare, finance, and manufacturing datasets for utility, distributional similarity, and privacy. CTGAN, described as using mode-specific normalization and a conditional generator, is run as one of the baseline oversampling methods (alongside SMOTE and ForestDiffusion) against which the proposed methods are compared on every dataset and ratio sweep.

preprint-evaluating-virtual-control-augm.summary: This preprint empirically tests whether completing prematurely-stopped control arms of randomized controlled trials with AI-generated 'virtual patients' can reproduce the treatment effect of the original, fully-recruited trial, using data from the IST and IST3 stroke trials. The authors train CTGAN and TVAE on recruited control patients, generate virtual controls to complete partially recruited arms, and show this can produce substantially biased or misleading treatment-effect estimates. Both generative architectures are implemented via the Synthetic Data Vault (SDV) library, with hyperparameters tuned and synthetic data quality assessed using SDMetrics' general score, making SDV's CTGAN and TVAE synthesizers the core generators underpinning the whole empirical study.

preprint-introspective-dynamic-model-glo.summary: This paper analyzes five months of job execution records from the PanDA workflow management system used by large high-energy-physics collaborations (ATLAS, Belle II, CMS, DUNE) to identify performance indicators like queuing time and error rate, and proposes building a generative AI model to simulate time series of computing payloads for 'what-if' resource-allocation scenario testing. CTGAN is cited only once in the introduction as background on deep generative models achieving competitive data-augmentation performance, alongside TabDDPM, with no code run or method adopted from it.

paper-xai-evaluate-synthetic-2025.summary: Turns synthetic-data evaluation into an explanation problem: a discriminator is trained to tell real records from synthetic ones, and feature importance, feature effect and counterfactual methods are then applied to that discriminator to say which columns, value ranges and interactions the generator got wrong, rather than returning a single quality score. CTGAN is one of six synthesizers whose detectability is compared, and the appendix works the full diagnosis through on ten CTGAN-generated nursery datasets.

preprint-deep-generative-framework-joint.summary: This paper proposes a VAE-based deep generative framework for synthesizing joint household-individual population datasets, introducing a new data structure to capture household-individual relationships, a transfer learning process aligning generated data with census tract marginals, and a decoupled binary cross-entropy loss for out-of-sample generation. It is evaluated on Delaware and North Carolina census data. In its related-work discussion of prior GAN-based population synthesis approaches, it cites Xu and Veeramachaneni's Tabular GAN (TGAN) work only in passing, without running it in the proposed framework.

preprint-convex-space-learning-tabular-2.summary: This preprint introduces NextConvGeN, a generator-discriminator architecture that extends the ConvGeN framework to generate entire synthetic tabular datasets by learning the convex space of local data neighborhoods, and benchmarks it against several state-of-the-art tabular synthesizers across ten biomedical datasets on utility and privacy metrics. CTGAN (and TVAE) are run unmodified as baseline generative models throughout the empirical comparison, evaluated on ML efficacy, distributional similarity, and privacy-attack resistance alongside NextConvGeN. SDV's CTGAN and TVAE are used as comparison baselines rather than being extended or run as the paper's own generator.

preprint-enhancing-bond-strength-predict.summary: This preprint proposes a machine-learning framework to predict bond strength at ultra-high-performance concrete (UHPC) to normal concrete (NC) interfaces, combining data augmentation with explainability techniques to improve predictive accuracy and interpretability given limited experimental data. The work targets structural/materials engineering applications in construction. TGAN, the SDV-family tabular synthesizer, is cited in connection with the paper's data augmentation approach, though it is unclear from the available evidence whether it was actually run to generate synthetic training data.

preprint-fedtabdiff-federated-learning-d.summary: This preprint proposes FedTabDiff, a federated learning extension of denoising diffusion probabilistic models for generating high-fidelity mixed-type synthetic tabular data across decentralized financial and medical datasets without centralizing sensitive records. It contributes a synchronous federated update and weighted-averaging scheme for training diffusion generators collaboratively while preserving privacy. CTGAN is cited only in related work as prior conditional-GAN tabular synthesis, while the SDV library (v1.3.0) is directly run to implement the machine-learning utility evaluation metrics used to score the generated synthetic data.

preprint-goal-recognition-design-general.summary: This preprint addresses goal recognition design (GRD), proposing a machine-learning framework that predicts worst-case distinctiveness (wcd) for a decision-making environment and an agent behavior model, then optimizes the environment via gradient-based methods to make goal inference easier and more scalable, including for suboptimal human agents. The paper's core contribution is unrelated to synthetic tabular data generation. CTGAN is cited only in the bibliography as prior work on modeling tabular data with conditional GANs, with no engagement in the body text.

preprint-retailsynth-synthetic-generatio.summary: This paper introduces RetailSynth, a multi-stage discrete-choice simulation environment for generating realistic synthetic grocery-shopping transactions to benchmark personalized pricing, promotion, and recommendation algorithms. The model is calibrated on public grocery data and used to analyze how different pricing policies affect revenue, category penetration, and customer retention. The Synthetic Data Vault is cited only in passing, alongside another reference, as an example of the broader trend toward generative modeling of raw tabular data, with no SDV code or model actually used in the work.

preprint-synthetic-applications-finance-.summary: A broad survey and applied report from J.P. Morgan AI Research covering synthetic data use cases across finance -- tabular, time-series, event-series, and unstructured data -- for fraud/AML, market simulation, customer journeys, and document generation, with attention to privacy, fairness, and regulatory compliance. In its fraud-detection case study the authors generate synthetic credit-card fraud data with GaussianCopula, CTGAN, CopulaGAN, and TVAE, comparing resulting class balance and downstream XGBoost AUROC across tuned and untuned settings. SDV's CTGAN, CopulaGAN, TVAE, and GaussianCopula synthesizers are run directly as the generators underpinning this empirical fraud-detection evaluation, and SDV itself is separately reviewed and compared against other synthetic-data libraries.

paper-gan-att-treatment-effect-2022.summary: Replaces the matching step in counterfactual inference with a generative one: two conditional GANs learn the joint densities of the treatment and control groups, conditional average treatment effects are read off as the difference between the two conditional densities at the same covariate value, and their ensemble average over the treated sample is the estimate of the average treatment effect on the treated, which sidesteps the sample dropping and lack of common support that matching suffers in high dimensions. CTGAN is the generator the estimator is built on, taken from its Python code as documented on sdv.dev and run with a single merged network conditioned on a treatment one-hot vector in place of two separate ones.

preprint-pca-utility-measure-synthetic-2.summary: This paper proposes a new utility measure for synthetic data evaluation that aggregates four popular utility metrics into a single score via principal component analysis, then tests whether this composite measure predicts real-world (ML) performance better than existing metrics. It compares four well-known synthetic data generators (DataSynthesizer, SDV, Synthpop parametric, Synthpop non-parametric) across multiple datasets on quality and stability metrics. The Synthetic Data Vault (SDV), described as modeling the population's joint distribution via a latent Gaussian copula, is run as one of the four synthesizers benchmarked throughout the empirical study.

paper-generative-trees-2022.summary: Develops a tree-based generative model for tabular data, deriving a variational GAN-style loss whose tightness follows from the properness of the supervised loss and the calibration property that decision trees satisfy, and giving both a boosting-compliant adversarial training algorithm and a copycat scheme in which the generator copies the discriminator's tree at run time and completes it. CTGAN is the single neural contender the empirical case is argued against, run at 10, 300 and 1000 epochs across the train-on-synthetic, synthetic-versus-real discrimination and data-augmentation experiments, with per-domain statistical win/tie/loss counts against it reported in Tables 3 and 4.

preprint-taxonomy-use-synthetic-advanced.summary: This preprint develops a taxonomy of synthetic data use in advanced analytics, categorizing generation approaches (domain knowledge, statistical distribution, deep learning) and identifying typical application scenarios such as sample generation, sample size augmentation, and anonymization, based on a systematic literature review. It aims to assess current adoption and highlight missed research opportunities rather than proposing or running any new synthesizer. The SDV paper is cited only as one of three supporting references for the claim that synthetic data can generate samples, augment data, or anonymize data.

preprint-generating-synthetic-but-plausi.summary: This paper proposes a method for generating synthetic binary healthcare datasets (ICD-9 diagnostic codes) using a latent variable moment-based learning approach, comparing it against MedGAN on realism metrics such as Random Forest discriminability and MMD, and arguing its outputs avoid GAN mode collapse while remaining more interpretable. The Synthetic Data Vault paper is cited only in the reference list, in a motivating remark about data sharing across healthcare organizations, with no SDV component run or engaged with in the body text. It is a bare bibliographic citation to the original SDV paper, not an implementation or benchmark use.

repo-piit.summary: Course material for a data-analyst bootcamp, spanning import, inspection and transformation of tabular data. A dedicated notebook teaches SDV, moving from the demo-dataset loader to `GaussianCopulaSynthesizer`. It records SDV entering an introductory analytics curriculum rather than a research setting.

repo-secure-and-private-ai-products-mast.summary: Course material for a masterclass on designing secure and private machine-learning systems and products. Its synthetic-data unit is taught on SDV end to end: the demo loader, `GaussianCopulaSynthesizer` and `run_diagnostic` all appear in the same notebook, so students learn generation and validation together.
